facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protestors at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he arrived at Kaluzhskaya Square to take part in the 'March of Millions' march.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he walked down Yakimanka Street to Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he passed the metal detectors at Bolotnaya Square and joined other protestors in front of the stage, where a rock group was performing.
According to the applicant, after finding the route to Malyy Kamenyy Bridge blocked, he walked back and stayed in the general area of Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, he was both angered and scared by the actions of the police and actively resisted.
The applicant was eventually seized by four police officers and escorted to a police car, which took him to a police station.

On 14 May 2012 the Justice of the Peace of the 100th Court Circuit of the Yakimanka District of Moscow found the applicant guilty of non-compliance with a lawful order by a police officer, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The applicant was sentenced by the Justice of the Peace of the 100th Court Circuit of the Yakimanka District of Moscow to detention of twenty-four hours for the administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
On 28 May 2012 the applicant was detained on suspicion of participation in acts of mass disorder on 6 May 2012.
On 28 May 2012 the applicant was detained on suspicion of committing violent acts against the police on 6 May 2012.
On 30 May 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered that the applicant be placed in pre-trial detention until 6 July 2012.
On 5 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).
On 5 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
On 21 February 2014 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant guilty as charged under Article 212 § 2 and Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
The applicant was sentenced to three years and seven months' imprisonment.

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder, accompanied by violence, riot, arson, destruction of property, the use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 3 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the instigation of the acts of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1, or the instigation of participation in such acts, or the instigation of violence against citizens, shall be punishable by a restriction of liberty for up to two years, or community service for up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for the same term.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence which does not endanger life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community service for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protestors at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
On 5 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).
On 5 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).

The ten defendants in the criminal case before the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow were charged with participation in acts of mass disorder and committing acts of violence against police officers.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the unidentified persons called those present at Bolotnaya Square to use violence, which led to mass disorder accompanied by the use of violence against public officials in connection with the performance of their duties and the destruction of property.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that participants of the acts of mass disorder threw chunks of tarmac, stones, sticks and other objects at the police, which hit them on various parts of their body.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered the meeting at Bolotnaya Square to finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, at around 7.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 groups of police officers started pushing into the crowd, forcing it apart by using their truncheons.
According to the applicant, protestors at Bolotnaya Square were surrounded and squeezed together by police officers.
According to the applicant, at some point he realised that he was facing the police line and that the police were using excessive force to arrest protestors.
According to the applicant, he was both angered and scared by the actions of the police and actively resisted.

The Justice of the Peace of the 100th Court Circuit of the Yakimanka District of Moscow established that after the meeting at Bolotnaya Square the applicant had shouted anti-government slogans, ignoring the lawful demands of the police to cease those acts.

The Justice of the Peace of the 100th Court Circuit of the Yakimanka District of Moscow established that the applicant had thrown objects at the police officers, including stones, flagpoles, empty plastic bottles, and pieces of asphalt.
The Justice of the Peace of the 100th Court Circuit of the Yakimanka District of Moscow established that the applicant had refused to proceed to the police van.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, referred to the gravity of the charges against the applicant.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, stated that if the applicant was at liberty he could co-ordinate his position with accomplices whose identities were still being established by the investigation.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, pointed out that the applicant had forcefully resisted the police officers during his arrest, which had led to them using force and handcuffs against him.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, relied on information obtained from undercover sources that the applicant had connections with football fans and groups of anarchists.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, concluded that there were sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant was likely to abscond, continue his criminal activity, threaten witnesses, destroy evidence or otherwise obstruct the course of the criminal proceedings.
The applicant was accused of active resistance to police officers on 6 May 2012.
The applicant was accused of participation in a group assault on a police officer whereby the applicant had allegedly pulled a protective helmet off the officer's head.
The applicant was accused of participation in a group assault on a police officer whereby the applicant had allegedly punched and kicked the officer on the head and body.
In the updated charges of 16 November 2012, it was specified that the applicant had struck the police officer once on the head.
In the updated charges of 16 November 2012, it was specified that the applicant had kicked the police officer once on the body while the officer was lying on the ground.
Police Officer K. testified that he had been carrying out an order to split the crowd up when someone had pulled at his bullet-proof vest.
Police Officer K. testified that he had fallen to the ground and someone had hit him several times and had taken off his anti-riot helmet.
Police Officer K. testified that as a result of his fall and the blows, he had sustained injuries.
Police Officer V.K. testified that the applicant had kicked an unidentified police officer.
Three police officers, examined as witnesses during the trial, stated that the applicant had resisted arrest by planting his feet firmly on the ground and attempting to escape.
Three police officers, examined as witnesses during the trial, stated that the applicant had uttered obscenities to the police officers and shouted at them.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant used violence against Police Officer K. which did not endanger his life or health.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant, together with other unidentified participants of acts of mass disorder, tore off Police Officer K.'s anti-riot helmet.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant punched Police Officer K.'s head at least once and kicked Police Officer K. on the body at least once when the latter was lying on the ground.

The applicant testified that he was scared, felt that his life was in danger, and while in a state of fury moved towards a police officer who happened to be Police Officer K., and then moved his leg towards the police officer who was getting up.
The applicant insisted at trial that he caused no injuries to the police officer and that his actions, provoked by panic, were taken in response to the events occurring around him.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it became apparent that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
